newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee races to 18-mth peak, July up 7.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee races to 18-mth peak, July up 7.6 pct.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures, triggered by a new rally in New York, raced to the highest level in 18 months on aggressive roaster price-fixing and short-covering.
Arabica futures on the New York market rocketed to a new 20-year peak of 291.25 cents a lb in the morning trade helped by manufacturer buying.
The roaster buying soon spread to London. The advance gained further momentum as the surge met with little origin offers.
Benchmark July finished a hefty $158 up at $2,260 a tonne, a level not seen since November 17, 1995 when it hit $2,270. Its intraday peak was $2,262.
The contract, which broke the previous resistance at $2,190, now looked set to challenge the next upside goal at $2,319, nearly 40 percent retracement from its lows in 1994.
Traders said despite today's blistering rally, robustas were not over-valued even at these levels.
"New York is tremendously overdone but people were still short of paper," said one.
London's most-active September surged $167 at $2,291 as long holders rolled forward their July position.
In the process, July's discount to September widened to $31 by the close from $19 on Tuesday.
Volume was an impressive 11,558 lots, centred again on July and September.
New York arabica futures notched up steep gains on panic buying helped by weather forecasts calling for below normal temperatures in top grower Brazil.
But private U.S. forecaster Weather Services Corp said no crop-damaging cold was expected.
The Brazilian weather is in traders' minds as the country enters the dangerous frost months in June and July.

"There is no doubt that (arabica) coffee is physically tight with stockpiles in both consumer and producer countries near 20-year lows, and this makes the market extremely prone to weather scares in Brazil, even at this early stage of the season," broker GNI said. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
